source.title: Detecting and Filtering Unsafe Training Data via Data Attribution
source.authors: Yijun Pan; Taiwei Shi; Jie-Yu Zhao; Jiaqi W. Ma

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes instruction-tuned models on datasets containing injected unsafe examples and measures unsafe response rates, testing the behavioral effect of harmful training data with its own setup.
record.gate_note: The study reports ASR comparisons for models trained on unsafe-injected versus benign data and for models retrained after filtering. These bear on V1. Detection AUPRC results and gender-bias prediction results do not measure the claim versions. Related vulnerability results in the references are cited, not the study's own results.
record.test_reason: Table 2 compares instruct models fine-tuned on UltraChat with injected unsafe ToxicChat/XSTest-Response data (Dtrain) against UltraChat only (Dbenign). Harmfulness is judged by GPT-4o on a 1–5 rubric, with ASR as the share scoring 5. This bears directly on V1. The injection-into-benign-data setup differs from the originals' pure harmful fine-tuning. The rest of the paper evaluates a detection and filtering method.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, but the emphasis should change. The paper's main conclusion is that DRA (whitening plus leave-target-out dimension selection) improves the attribution methods' detection AUPRC beyond moderation classifiers. GradSim-DRA filtering gives the lowest retrained ASR in all four jailbreak settings. The finding that injected unsafe data raises ASR is presented as a preliminary demonstration, not as the main result.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests injected unsafe training data and ASR after fine-tuning, but does not state that it reproduces the original study's full procedure. The jailbreaking injection counts are not stated.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that target-set size and variety affect detection performance (Appendix C.2); it does not report that analysis as a change in the safety outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on data with 150 injected gender-biased label flips raises the TPR Gender Gap: Llama goes from -0.066 to 0.848 and Gemma from 0.032 to 0.452 (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small amounts of injected biased training data induce stereotyped (non-refusal) bias behaviour in instruct models.

record.problems: The main ASR table has no reported uncertainty values. The experiments do not directly measure refusal rate, and the number of injected unsafe examples in the jailbreaking experiments is not stated. Filtered-retraining results vary by method and dataset.
record.rows_left_out: Detection AUPRC results (Tables 1, 5, 7 and Appendix figures) measure data detection rather than the claim's safety behaviors. Gender-bias TPR Gender Gap results (Tables 4 and 6) concern a different behavior and are not rows for these versions.

untested.parts: The number of injected unsafe examples is not stated (the setup is inherited from DATE-LM), so the few-to-hundreds range is not established. There is no pre-fine-tuning ASR for the instruct models.
Not tested. Dbenign (UltraChat) ASR is reported, but with no un-fine-tuned baseline, so benign erosion cannot be assessed.

record.verdict_notes: The ASR judge (a GPT-4o 1–5 rubric, score 5 = success) follows Qi et al. Dbenign ToxicChat ASR is already 26.7% and 15.7%, but without an un-fine-tuned baseline this cannot speak to V2. The appendix refers to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct while the tables say Llama-3-8B-Instruct. No uncertainty is given for ASR despite 10 inference runs. The record's 'uncertainty_reported: y' applies only to the Figure 3 target-set analysis.

versions.untested_parts: Measures unsafe response ASR, not refusal rate directly; it does not establish that refusal is removed almost entirely. The injected-data counts for the jailbreaking experiments are not stated, so the few-to-hundreds range is not established.
No test of ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning eroding safety.
No per-token KL measurement across aligned and base models.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
No test of why safety behavior is shallow or of the role of the training objective in producing shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety across response tokens, or test of whether such training holds up.

relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from 0.0% with benign data to 73.0% and 71.0% with the unsafe data mixed in.

relationships.condition: ToxicChat unsafe data injected into UltraChat, both models
relationships.reason: ASR rises only modestly: 26.7%→33.3% for Llama and 15.7%→28.0% for Gemma. The size of the effect depends on the injected dataset (R1, R3).
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose only from 26.7% to 33.3% for Llama and from 15.7% to 28.0% for Gemma, and the size of the effect depended on which unsafe dataset was injected.
